faq: Do you open the account for me?
You open it, because eBay needs your identity and payout details, and we guide each step on screen or by message. Then you give us account access from your eBay settings and we do the rest.
Can you enter my bank details?
No. You enter payout, tax and identity details yourself, because they are private. We show you where each item goes and check the rest of the settings.
Will you help with selling limits?
We explain how eBay limits new sellers and how limits rise as you sell well. We do not use ways to get around limits, because that breaks eBay's rules. Good listings and on-time shipping are the way.

eBay charges you directly: final value fees on sales, and possibly insertion fees and ad fees. Our price covers setup only, and our checklist explains each fee type with a link to eBay's current rates.
desc:
A proper eBay seller account setup and launch plan gets you ready to list without avoidable account problems. Ecom Swift LLC guides you through seller type, business policies, shipping and return settings and a safe launch checklist, all inside your own eBay account.

## What is an eBay seller account setup?

An eBay seller account setup is the work of turning a basic eBay login into an account that is ready to sell. It covers the choice between a personal and a business seller, the payout and identity steps that eBay requires, and the business policies that every listing will use. Done well, it means your first listing can go live without stopping to fix settings.

You complete identity and payout steps yourself, because they involve your private details. We prepare everything around them and tell you exactly what to expect on each screen.

## Why a careful start matters on eBay

New sellers often rush to publish a listing and discover problems afterward. A missing return policy, a shipping setting that does not match the item or a misunderstood selling limit can block a listing or lead to a bad first sale. Early mistakes also feed into your seller record, which buyers and eBay both look at.

A calm start is cheaper than a repair. When policies, handling times and return terms are set once at account level, every later listing inherits them. That saves time on each item and keeps your promises to buyers consistent.

## How setup affects your first sales

Buyers on eBay compare many sellers for the same kind of item. They read shipping times, return terms and feedback before they click Buy. A new account with clear policies and honest handling times looks organized, and that lowers the doubt a buyer feels about a seller with no history.

Setup also affects how smoothly orders move. If your shipping policy matches your real packing routine, you ship when you said you would. Reliable shipping is how a new seller builds feedback, and feedback is what makes the next sale easier. We cannot control demand or competition, but we can remove the account-level reasons a first sale goes wrong.

## What a ready eBay seller account includes

- A seller type chosen on purpose, personal or business, with the reasons written down.
- Payment, shipping and return business policies created and named clearly.
- Handling time that matches how fast you can really pack and post.
- Domestic and international shipping options that suit your items.
- A return policy written in plain words that buyers can follow.
- Your seller dashboard explained, including Orders, Listings and Performance.
- Selling limits explained, so you know what to expect while the account is new.
- A shortlist of first items chosen for a safe start.
- A launch checklist covering feedback, messages and payout timing.

## What we do

We start with a short conversation about what you plan to sell, where you ship from and how you pack. From that we recommend a seller type and explain what changes between personal and business selling. You then complete the identity and payout steps on eBay's own pages, and we stay available to answer questions about what each screen means.

Next we build your business policies. In the Basic package that means payment, shipping and return policies applied as defaults. In the Standard and Premium packages we also create your first listings, set policies per item type, and explain selling limits and the payout and tax steps in general terms. The Premium package ends with a safe-start plan for the first month and a handover call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Use your real name and details exactly as they appear on your identity documents.
- Start with a few items you can describe accurately and ship quickly.
- Keep handling times honest, even if a shorter promise looks tempting.
- Read the launch checklist before you publish your first listing.
- Keep your own notes on every setting we explain.

**Avoid:**
- Opening several accounts to get around a limit.
- Listing items you do not yet hold or cannot source.
- Copying another seller's text or photos.
- Sharing your login with a helper instead of using proper access.
- Raising prices or volume sharply before the account has a record.

## Who this is for

This service suits a first-time seller who wants to start on eBay without guessing at settings. It also suits a small shop owner adding eBay as a second channel next to their own store, and a person clearing a collection who wants the account to look like a real business from the first listing.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you sell, where you ship from, how you pack and which seller type you lean towards. Send photos and details for your first items if your package includes listings. You keep control of your own identity and payout steps. We never ask for your password, and where eBay offers delegated or account access, you grant it to us as a limited user rather than sharing a login.
